title: Performance-Driven Pre-Assignment Routing for High-Speed Package Designs
problem: High-speed package routing lacks performance-driven optimization that minimizes critical path while preventing wire crossings within single metal layers.
motivation: Package routing optimization is essential for high-speed circuit performance without excessive overhead in wire length.
method: Dynamic programming—an optimization technique that builds solutions from smaller pieces—creates a baseline routing solution. A search algorithm then explores different orderings for routing individual signals through the package. It keeps only the promising options, finding an ordering that shortens the longest signal path (called the critical path) without allowing wires to cross on the same metal layer.
key_novelty: It combines dynamic programming baseline routing with search-based signal reordering to minimize the critical path while preventing wire crossings.
contributions: Novel dynamic programming method for baseline routing generation
Search-based optimization with effective pruning techniques
32.9% critical path reduction with minimal total path increase

metrics.ppa: 32.9% critical path reduction, 0.6% total path increase

limitations: Specific to package-level routing; single metal layer constraint; evaluation on five industrial designs.
